articles.title: IMF advises India to let rupee move as first defence amid oil shock
articles.excerpt:
istock photo for BL | Photo Credit: Dmitriy Razinkov

India should allow the dollar-rupee exchange rate to move as the first line of defence amid the ongoing oil shock, an IMF official said on Wednesday.

“Our advice to countries is to use the exchange rate as the first line of defence amid ongoing shocks,” Krishna Srinivasan, Director of the Asia and Pacific Department at the IMF, said at a media briefing in Mumbai. “We would advise India to let the exchange rate move.”

The Reserve Bank of India has intervened heavily to support the rupee via dollar sales from its reserves, a special window to offer dollars to oil companies and reserve requirements for large hedge requirements.

articles.title: Treasuries Slide After Middle East Strife Report Spurs Oil Gains
articles.excerpt:
(Bloomberg) -- Treasuries fell after reports suggesting the Middle East war is heating up lifted oil prices.

The selloff lifted yields across maturities to session highs, with short-term tenors rising most. The two-year note’s climbed as much as five basis points to 4.83%, the highest level in a week. The US dollar strengthened.

After having been moribund for much of the session, Treasuries were hit at around 2:45 p.m. New York time, concurrently with US stock indexes, as West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures jumped to about $98.50 a barrel from $97.
